name: Airtel Africa
source: Airtel Africa plc audited annual consolidated financial statements and Q4/FY2026 investor results pack for the year ended 31 March 2026 (airtel.africa investor relations; annual report note 14 for EPS). All money rows stored in ABSOLUTE US dollars: the source prints US$ millions, so each printed figure is multiplied by 1,000,000 here (previous stored copies held the printed millions and rendered as thousands in the panel). EPS is in US cents as printed. Revenue US$6,415m, operating profit US$2,115m, total finance costs US$713m, profit before tax US$1,419m, income tax US$606m, profit after tax US$813m, basic EPS 18.6 cents.

rows.label: Non-current Assets
rows.source: Airtel Africa plc audited results for the year ended 31 March 2026, consolidated statement of financial position, printed pages 24 and 25 (file _ngx_pdf/AIRTELAFRI.pdf); US$ millions. Non-current assets 11,058 (31 Mar 2025: 9,862); current assets 2,905 (2,161); current liabilities 4,992 (4,242); non-current liabilities 5,483 (5,006). The statement also prints net current liabilities of (2,087) / (2,081), which 2,905 - 4,992 reproduces exactly.

periods_note: columns dropped: FY2024, FY2023, FY2022 - no row in this file carries a figure for them, so they rendered as pure dashes
currencyNote: Airtel Africa reports in US dollars; the NGX doclib filing it is taken from is a USD statement. The share price quoted on the NGX is in naira and that is correct in the market record - only the statements are USD. Corrected because mixing a naira price with dollar earnings misstates every ratio by roughly the exchange rate.
